You're invited!

Come ride with us
to the North Pole.

One night in December, we're getting on a train together and riding out into the dark to find the North Pole. We'd love for you and your kids to be on it.

Here's how it goes: everybody piles into one big decorated train car, the whistle blows, and off we go. Cookies and hot chocolate come around while Christmas music plays. Then the train stops — we're there — and Santa gets on and comes down the aisle to visit every single kid.

It's about an hour and a half of pure Christmas. Bring the whole family.

Wear the ugly sweater. Bring the camera. Come hungry.

The plan

How the night goes

Roughly. The train leaves at 5:00 sharp, so the trick is just getting there early enough to relax before it does.

3:00 PM

Head out

The drive is about an hour and five minutes for most of us, but December traffic on I-8 can add a good half hour. Leaving at 3:00 means you're not stressed.

4:15 PM

Get there and find us

Park, stretch your legs, say hi to everybody, and get some pictures while there's still a little light out.

ParkSay hiPictures
4:45 PM

Time to get on the train!

Everybody find a seat. This is the one time of the night to hurry.

5:00 PM

All aboard — here we go

The whistle blows and we pull out. Cookies and hot chocolate start coming around, the music starts, and it's dark out the windows already.

CocoaCookiesMusicStories
~5:45 PM

We made it to the North Pole

The train stops. Santa gets on. He comes right down the aisle and talks to every kid — no line, no rushing, no waiting your turn behind strangers.

~6:30 PM

Back at the station

Hugs in the parking lot and a very quiet drive home with sleepy kids in the back seat.

The best part

Santa gets on the train

When we stop at the North Pole, Santa comes aboard and works his way down the aisle. He sits with every kid, asks them what they're hoping for, and stays as long as they want to talk. No line to stand in, nobody rushing you along. Have your camera ready — you'll want this one.

A peek inside

This is the train car

Look at it. Garland on every window, little lamps, big soft seats, stockings on the wall, and a Christmas tree in the corner. Wait until the kids see it.

Map goes here

It's cold out there — for real

Campo is up at 2,600 feet, so once the sun goes down it's a lot colder than home — often down in the 30s by the time we're heading back. The train car itself is heated and cozy. Outside it is not. Bring the coats, especially for the kids.

What to bring

  • Warm jacket
  • Camera or phone
  • Christmas sweater
  • Holiday pajamas
  • Comfortable shoes
  • Snacks
  • Water
  • Gloves for the kids
  • Christmas spirit

Good questions

Stuff people have asked us

How long are we on the train?

About 90 minutes. We leave at 5:00 and we're back at the station around 6:30, so you'll be home at a reasonable hour.

What should we wear?

Go all out. Ugly Christmas sweaters, Christmas pajamas, matching family outfits, light-up reindeer antlers — all of it is welcome and all of it will end up in photos. Just bring a warm jacket too.

Is it warm inside the train?

Yep, it's enclosed and heated. You're only out in the cold while we're getting on and taking pictures.

Can we bring snacks?

Sure. Snacks and non-alcoholic drinks are fine to bring. Cookies and hot chocolate are already taken care of. No alcohol unless it's cleared with the museum ahead of time.

Do the kids get pictures with Santa?

Yes! Santa comes to every family right at their seats. No line, no photo fee, nobody hurrying you. Take as many as you want.

Will little kids like it?

This whole thing is made for them. One tip from experience: it's a late night for the little ones, so an afternoon nap goes a long way.

Is there a bathroom?

There are restrooms at the station — send everybody before we get on, since we're on the train for about 90 minutes.

What if it rains?

We still go! Bring a jacket with a hood instead of an umbrella — it gets breezy out on the platform.

Can we bring a friend?

Ask us first — there are only so many seats on the car and we have to give a final headcount. If there's room we'd love to have them.

A few quick things
  • Be there by 4:15. The train really does leave at 5:00 without us.
  • Keep the kids with a grown-up — there are real trains moving around.
  • Stick with the group once we're at the station.
  • Be gentle with the train car. It's older than all of us.
  • No alcohol unless it's arranged with the museum first.
  • Have an unreasonable amount of fun.
